transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check today. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes, I have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! You can start doing light exercise like gardening from 1 week after your surgery. 

However, you should avoid strenuous or heavy exercise, and also avoid swimming for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you. My next question is: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some mild sensitivity to bright light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. We'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if the light sensitivity is severe or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. 

Are you experiencing severe sensitivity or redness and pain?
transcript.delivered: Some mild sensitivity to bright light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.text:
However, if the light sensitivity is severe or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, just one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago. Thanks for all the information. I don't have any more questions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
